title: A 40-day input advance permits positive response fits within 0.4 percent fluence for two median ASASSN-14ko UV profiles
abstract: We test whether positive stationary smoothing can change a narrow ASASSN-14ko UV flare into broad cycles 28 and 29 when the input can arrive earlier. We use published UVW2 profile samples, positive-kernel fits, and a cumulative bound that also applies to time-dependent passive release. For reference cycle 21 and median profile parameters, a maximum 40-day input advance gives total variation distances of 0.333 and 0.153 percent of fluence. A finer grid gives 0.207 and 0.010 percent. At 1 percent distance tolerance, a necessary advance bound has median 28.1 days for cycle 28 and 13.5 days for cycle 29, with conditional central 95 percent ranges of 18.6-34.1 and 6.5-22.9 days. Some cycle-29 posterior shapes still fit poorly. Thus fixed-clock delay failure does not exclude all positive response models; earlier input is a quantified cost of an allowed escape. The result depends on fitted UV profiles and extrapolated tails. No new observation, physical reservoir or orbital history is established.

display.caption: Necessary earlier input for any passive allocation at a 1 percent profile-distance tolerance. Intervals are conditional on published UV fits.
